## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components, combined with a fused framebuffer scatter, can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈949 is below the smallest measured point (N=4000). At q=0.01, ns/p FALLS from 11.334 (N=4000) to 8.039 (N=16000) — overhead amortization. Crossing the L2 spill at N≈60787, cost FALLS slightly to 7.895 (N=65000), then is FLAT at 7.80 through N=4M — no L2→DRAM knee. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: the plateau shifts from 7.80 (q=0.01) to 8.27 (q=0.05) to 10.49 (q=0.25), preserving the amortize-then-flat shape throughout.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.85 GB/s at N≥1M, q=0.01 — 35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. Overhead-bound at small N (6.09 GB/s at N=4000), the algo reaches a compute/overhead-bound plateau by N=16000 and never becomes bandwidth-bound. Death rate degrades the plateau: 8.85 → 8.34 → 6.57 GB/s as q rises 0.01 → 0.25. It falls far short of the ceiling in every regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. The update loop loads 4 floats with `ldur q16`, rearranges via `ext.16b` and `mov.s v18[3]`, then applies `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` and `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s`, writing back with `stur q7`/`str d7`. A gather is present: `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x10]`. The fused scatter is scalar: `fcvtzs` converts positions, `csel` clamps, and 22 `strb`/13 `ldrb` perform byte-granular random framebuffer writes. These byte stores, plus `bl _layouts.ML01.data.Data.spawn` on respawn, explain the 35%-of-ceiling cap — the update streams but the scatter cannot.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak 8.85 GB/s is 35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling at best (q=0.01, large N), falling to 26% (6.57 GB/s) at q=0.25. Auto-vectorization across components (`fmul.4s`, `fadd.4s`) streamlines the update, but the fused scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes cap bandwidth far below the streaming ceiling regardless of death rate.
